newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan August gold imports fall 59 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan August gold imports fall 59 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's imports of gold bars, coins and plate fell sharply to 2.882 tonnes in August from 7.093 tonnes a year earlier, the Finance Ministry said on Saturday.
The imports were also down on a month-on-month basis, compared with 4.602 tonnes in July.
Gold traders attributed the fall in imports to seasonal adjustment and easing tensions with China.

Gold imports have been falling since March when the island bought a record 25.238 tonnes as China conducted war games in the Taiwan Strait during the run-up to the island's historic persidential elections on March 23.

Gold is traditionally considered a safe haven in times of uncertainty. Taiwanese began to buy gold heavily from mid-1995 when China conducted a missile test near Taiwan to warn the island not to raise its international profile.
The ministry said Taiwan's gold exports in August remained small at 0.19 tonnes, down from 0.253 tonnes in August 1995.
